transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-26 15:00 PDT / Duration ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Celine Park (Aperture Procurement), Tom O'Rourke (Security), Anya Feldman (Legal), Marta Ruiz (Cloud Ops)

Summary: Quick procurement + security preflight for onboarding Aperture Health. Focus areas: SLA routing and tiers, Dedicated vs Hosted economics for high-throughput inference, DPA/MSA redline concerns (data retention & audit logs), KMS BYOK/HSM requirements, network peering/VPC preflight, pilot scope and success metrics.

Topics: SLA targets, dedicated capacity pilot, BYOK/HSM flow, egress/egress-fee language, DPA redlines, benchmark plan, next steps

00:00:10 Jordan (Redwood): ok hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday, we'll kick off with a brief agenda — procurement and security routing, the sla sprint for your side, and then a quick KMS preflight. is that still right, celine?
00:00:22 Celine (Aperture): yes thanks jordan. we wanted to make sure we don't miss the billing lane and the data residency points, those are big for our compliance board.
00:00:31 Jordan: great, super. priya i'll hand to you for a quick tech recap of what redwood will give in a dedicated pilot.
00:00:39 Priya (Redwood SE): yeah, quick overview — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with a pinned throughput target. we expose model routing policies — so you can route by latency SLO or cost SLO, and we have automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants. for the pilot we recommend continuous KV cache warmup, and we'll turn on prefix caching to keep latency down. note: our runtime supports BYOK via HSM-backed KMS for private deployments, and for hosted we can do customer-managed keys via our KMS integration.
00:01:05 Tom (Aperture): couple quick questions — one is egress. our finance folks are worried about unpredictable egress fees if we run a high volume. how do you typically bill egress, and can we cap it or get an estimate?
00:01:18 Jordan: good question. standard hosted pricing includes egress inside the per-token line item for API responses up to X, but if you do private peering or bring-your-own-infra there can be network egress fees from cloud providers. for Dedicated we can model expected egress based on request volume, and for the pilot we'll surface monthly egress estimates in the pricing matrix. also we can add a cap in the contract but that tends to be a commercial concession — we'll put options in the pricing doc.
00:01:44 Anya (Aperture Legal): on the MSA/DPA side, we have three high-level asks: first, 1) max data retention for inference logs and debug traces (we want 90 days default), 2) audit log integrity and tamper-evidence, and 3) clear SOC2/ISO artifacts. are these covered in your standard DPA?
00:02:02 Jordan: yes our standard DPA includes retention and audit log provisions, but we can review redlines. priya can you flag the location of the audit log and retention controls in the security deck?
00:02:11 Priya: yep — it's in the security appendix, section 3.2 on audit and section 4 on retention. caveat: the retention TTL for cached prefixes is different from stored logs, so we'll call that out. also note the "KV cache" sometimes transcribed in folks' docs as K V cache — small transcription issue but important since it's an in-memory cache not part of logs.
00:02:33 Marta (Aperture): for BYOK — we need HSM-backed keys and monthly rotation, plus proof of key origin. can you support Hardware Security Module (HSM) and do we get attestation?
00:02:45 Marco (Redwood): yes we support BYOK for Redwood Private and Dedicated with HSM integrations (we support external KMS providers like AWS KMS with CloudHSM or customer HSM through our key connector). attestation docs and a key rotation playbook can be shared — the attestation is a standard HSM cert, but some customers want extra audit trails; we can include that in the compliance package.
00:03:06 Tom: ok note, we will likely require monthly rotation and a signed attestation at onboarding.
00:03:12 Celine: procurement question — if we start Dedicated pilot, what's the minimum commit and how flexible is it to convert to reserved capacity?
00:03:20 Jordan: pilot is typically 6 weeks with a short trial commit (we can do a trial consumption cap). if you like results, we offer a reserved capacity term — 3/6/12 month blocks. pricing for reserved gives discounts over pay-as-you-go. we'll lay out the conversion path in the pricing matrix.
00:03:35 Anya: there are a few DPA clauses we think are non-negotiable: no sub-processing without notice, and a data residency clause that data at rest in eu regions only if we choose eu. also need to understand your anomaly detection alerts for data exfil patterns.
00:03:51 Priya: we have alert hooks that can be routed to your security console; we can send sample alert webhook schema. redwood also supports region pinning per model endpoint so you can keep inference in eu region.
00:04:05 Jordan: can i ask — are you planning to use the embeddings route or the chat/generation route for the high-volume flows? that's relevant for token patterns and cost modeling.
00:04:14 Celine: both, actually. search embeddings for semantic search are heavy, and also a chat feature for support automation. so we need both embeddings and generation estimates.
00:04:24 Priya: good to know. embeddings often have different batching characteristics — we'll include separate cost model lines. for embeddings we can recommend larger batching and more aggressive quantization profiles to save cost.
00:04:36 Tom: technical deep dive — network wise we want to do VPC peering into your Private control plane. is that supported? any ports we need to open?
00:04:46 Marco: yes VPC peering supported. we'll send a preflight checklist: expected peering CIDR ranges, minimal egress firewall rules (TCP 443 outbound for control plane, optional ports for metrics), and an optional test VM that you can use to validate MTU and latency.
00:05:05 Marta: perfect, we'll get that to our cloud team.
00:05:08 Jordan: quick callout — backlog of procurement approvals sometimes stalls on the escrow/escape clauses. aperture, do you require code escrow or model escrow?
00:05:18 Anya: model escrow is unlikely, but we want a rollback / escape clause if there's sustained SLA breaches for more than 72 hours with no mitigation path.
00:05:27 Jordan: understood. our standard SLA includes a remediation plan and credits, but we can add an escalated termination right on sustained unmitigated outage >72h for enterprise contracts. we'll mark as legal discuss.
00:05:38 Celine: on success metrics for the pilot — we need 3 things: 1) p95 latency under 300ms for generation at typical load, 2) cost per 1M tokens below a threshold (we'll supply target), 3) no PII leakage incidents in eval prompts.
00:05:53 Priya: we can instrument p95 and token counts in the console and provide a dashboard. for PII leakage we'll run targeted evals with your test prompt suite. can you share the prompt suite or a sanitized extract?
00:06:06 Celine: yes we'll sanitize and send — expecting to send by monday.
00:06:10 Jordan: perfect.
00:06:13 Tom: small nit — audit logs: do you provide immutable storage or object versioning for logs? we need tamper-evident chain.
00:06:21 Marco: audit logs can be pushed to your S3 with object-lock or to our audit log retention bucket with WORM settings. we'll provide both options; if you want third-party attestations that's also available as an addon.
00:06:36 Anya: also please note we will require a clause about breach notification timelines — 72 hours is our expectation.
00:06:43 Jordan: standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents; we'll surface that clause in the MSA.
00:06:48 Celine: let's talk pricing approvals — finance needs a one-pager comparing hosted vs dedicated, with committed discount levels and egress assumptions. can you do that?
00:06:57 Jordan: yes, pricing one-pager + conversion flow. i'll include an annex for egress modeling.
00:07:03 Priya: bumping back to the pilot scope — our recommendation: 6-week Dedicated pilot, BYOK HSM test in week 2, run two benchmark profiles (embeddings heavy, chat heavy), and then a final readout with dashboards. that should give you the perf and cost signals.
00:07:20 Marta: from ops side we want to see the HSM attestation and confirm rotation automation hooks.
00:07:26 Marco: ok we'll include the attestation doc and rotation playbook.
00:07:30 Anya: legal redlines note — we will push to shorten your indemnity carveouts around third-party claims related to data processing; that's a negotiation point.
00:07:38 Jordan: understood, we'll take that back to our legal team.
00:07:42 Celine: operational question — how do you handle rollbacks if a new model rollout causes a regression in quality? we need automatic fallback to a pinned version.
00:07:52 Priya: rollouts support canary and immediate rollback; you can pin endpoints to specific model versions, and our routing policy can fallback to a compatible variant if capacity problems show up. we also provide automatic regression alerts tied to evals.
00:08:07 Tom: one more security check — do you sign a confidentiality addendum for logs that contain PHI?
00:08:15 Jordan: yes we have a PHI addendum and can put extra controls under our Private deployment or VPC option. we'll add that as an optional annex.
00:08:23 Anya: perfect.
00:08:26 Jordan: wrap up — let's recap next steps: we'll send pricing + SLA one-pager, priya uploads benchmark runbook, we get DPA redlines from Anya, aperture ops send peering info and HSM policy. target kickoff for pilot week of 2025-07-07.
00:08:40 Celine: thanks everyone.
00:08:43 Jordan: thanks all.

Action items (transcript): Jordan to send pricing + SLA one-pager; Priya to share runbook; Anya to send DPA redlines; Tom/Marta to provide peering CIDR and HSM policy.

References shared during call: pricing template (link: https://tinyurl.com/redwood-pricing-aperture), security appendix (link: https://redwood.docs/security-appendix), benchmark runbook (to be shared to the team drive), sample alert webhook schema (file: alert-webhook-schema.json).

End of transcript.
